# Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

Chain-of-thought reasoning is a framework in which LLMs decompose complex tasks into a series of intermediate steps, often articulated as natural language rationales, before producing a final answer. Through [prompting techniques](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/prompting-techniques) that supply examples with explicit reasoning sequences, LLMs can be induced to generate analogous stepwise reasoning at inference time, thereby enhancing their ability to tackle multi-step mathematical, commonsense, symbolic, and other high-complexity problems. The chain-of-thought approach not only boosts performance on many benchmarks but also renders the reasoning process more interpretable and potentially amenable to inspection and verification.

This report investigates Chain-of-Thought prompting, a technique that encourages a large language model (LLM) to"think step by step"(Wei et al., 2022), and finds that many recent models perform some form of CoT reasoning even if not asked. This report investigates two commonly held prompting beliefs: a) offering to tip the AI model and b) threatening the AI model and demonstrates two things that suggest simple prompting variations
